newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end lower with Tokyo shares.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end lower with Tokyo shares.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei stock index futures ended weaker on Tuesday, tracking the sharp fall in Tokyo share prices in relatively active pre-Christmas trade.
The March Nikkei contract finished at 19,240, down 355 points on a total volume of 11,000 contracts.
Traders said the market opened slightly above its previous close but backed off from a session high of 19,685 when a major commission house sold heavily mid-morning.
"Majors probably sold the market on the BOJ's cut in issues basis," a commission house dealer said, referring to the Bank of Japan's cut in bond purchases on Tuesday morning.
The BOJ bought bonds worth only 100 billion yen compared with the usual 200 billion yen.
Sentiment turned increasingly bearish on moderate turnover with locals jumping into the fray as prices headed south.
Some traders predicted that Nikkei futures, devoid of major institutional participants over the Christmas week, would be led by local dealers and could drift toward 18,500.
Tokyo stocks plunged on worries that Japan's economic prospects remained bleak, causing the key Nikkei cash index in Tokyo to slip to a 12-month low at 19,161.71.
